summary: Russian forces launched a massive overnight combined drone and missile barrage across Ukraine, including ballistic missiles from Voronezh and Kalibr cruise missiles from the Caspian Sea, targeting Kyiv, Zaporizhzhia, Dnipropetrovsk, and multiple other regions. Ukrainian strikes hit a Moscow oil refinery, a Kastus radar system, UAV control points, and a primary Russian reactive drone launch base in Donetsk region. Russian Geran-type drone production is slated to expand by approximately 28,000 units annually by 2029, while Ukraine has lost over 600 locomotives since February 2022.

sections.executive_summary: Russian forces executed a large-scale overnight combined drone and missile attack across Ukraine, employing ballistic missiles from Voronezh and Kalibr cruise missiles from the Caspian Sea against Kyiv, Zaporizhzhia, Dnipropetrovsk, and other regions. Ukrainian defenses reported striking a Moscow oil refinery, a Kastus radar, UAV control points, and a primary Russian reactive drone launch base in Donetsk region. Russian Geran-type drone production is set to expand by approximately 28,000 units annually by 2029, while Ukraine has lost over 600 locomotives since 2022 and faces monthly casualties estimated at 27,000 by Polish leadership.

sections.threat_assessment: Russia is intensifying long-range strike capabilities with combined ballistic and cruise missile barrages from Voronezh and the Caspian Sea, complemented by mass Shahed drone swarms transiting multiple axes to saturate Ukrainian air defenses. The expansion of Geran drone production to potentially 64,000 units annually by 2029 signals a sustained aerial attrition strategy. Ukrainian counterstrikes on Russian energy and C4ISR nodes (Moscow refinery, Kastus radar, drone launch base) demonstrate growing deep-strike capacity, but the 27,000 monthly casualty rate and 600+ locomotive losses indicate severe manpower and logistics strain. The Trump-Zelensky dynamic introduces diplomatic uncertainty regarding strike permissions on Russian energy infrastructure.
sections.regional_response: EU intelligence services formally acknowledge hybrid threats from Russia, citing documented drone incursions near European airports. Polish leadership publicly disclosed Ukrainian casualty figures (27,000/month) and frames Ukraine as a functional ally keeping Russian forces distant from NATO borders. Estonian Defense Minister Herem issued explicit threats to destroy Russian infrastructure and disintegrate the Russian state. These statements reflect hardening Eastern European resolve but also risk escalating rhetoric beyond kinetic coordination.
sections.intelligence_notes: The simultaneous Kalibr launches from the Caspian and ballistic missiles from Voronezh suggest coordinated multi-axis strike planning, possibly testing Ukrainian air defense coordination across northern, central, and southern sectors. Shahed transit through the Chornobyl exclusion zone indicates Russian willingness to risk radiological incidents for route optimization. The 11:1 and 19:1 body exchange ratios, if accurate, imply asymmetric attrition favoring Russia, though verification remains difficult. Ukrainian rail degradation (600+ locomotives lost) critically undermines sustainment and mobilization logistics. The Trump request to halt refinery strikes may foreshadow U.S. pressure on Ukrainian targeting policy.
